title: Open Concept Renovations in Westchester: What You Need to Know Before Starting
excerpt: An open concept layout can transform how your family lives in your home. Here's what to expect when you're planning this kind of renovation in Westchester County.
content:
The appeal of an open concept home is real. You want your kitchen connected to your living room. You want to see into the dining area while you cook. You want natural light flowing through the entire space instead of getting trapped behind walls.

But knocking down a wall isn't like removing drywall. It's structural work. It requires planning. It requires someone who knows how to do it right.

Why Open Concept Renovations Are More Complex Than They Look

When you remove a wall in your Westchester home, you're often removing a load-bearing wall. That wall holds up the structure above it. Take it away without proper support, and you create a serious problem. You need a licensed architect in New York to evaluate the wall and design a solution that works. You also need a general contractor in Westchester who understands how to execute that design properly.

This is where design-build firms have an advantage. When your architect is also your general contractor, you avoid the miscommunication that happens when two separate companies interpret the plans differently. Silvio M. Luca, principal at House Architecture & Construction, PLLC, handles both roles on every project he takes on. He's a licensed New York State architect and a licensed general contractor working in communities like Scarsdale, Mamaroneck, and White Plains. That means he's the one making decisions on your job site, not delegating to someone else.

What the Permitting Process Looks Like

Here's something homeowners often miss: every town in Westchester County has its own building department. Rye has one. Pelham has one. Tarrytown has one. Each one reviews permits slightly differently, though the rules are similar. Your residential architect in Westchester needs to understand the specific requirements for your municipality before submitting drawings.

Delays happen when architects don't know these local details. Revisions get requested. Plans go back and forth. On a design-build project, having one firm handle both the architecture and the construction means someone's paying close attention to these requirements from day one.

Planning a Home Addition With Your Open Concept

Many homeowners in Harrison, Dobbs Ferry, and Bronxville combine an open concept conversion with a home addition. You tear down the wall, and you add square footage to make the space feel even bigger. This requires coordinating structural work, HVAC systems, electrical service, and more.

Planning a home addition in Westchester County requires someone who understands building codes, load paths, and how to tie new construction into existing framing. You need a firm that can design the addition, get permits from your local building department, and then build it correctly. That's where having a licensed architect based in Westchester who also holds a general contractor license makes a difference.
